posts.author: Pianomaxx
posts.content_md:
Hello Holographers,

I would like to create a motive for a Denisyuk hologram, made of a box of gelatin, and put small objects in there, so that the objects would appear to fly in space. Did anyone of you try this before? I am a bit sceptical about possible diffraction effects or intensity losses through the gelatin.

best regards,

Max

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
Motive? 

Shine your laser on the gelatin and see what happens. Also use some polarizing film (sunglasses work fine) to see what it does to the polarization.

The only real problem I can think of that's all that likely is movement in the gelatin due to evaporation but if you cover it that should be minimized.

Give it a shot, the results could be interesting.

(btw, if the goal is things flying in space you could achieve similar results by supporting the objects from behind)

posts.author: Pianomaxx
posts.content_md:
Excuse me, of course I meant "scene", not "motive", got the wrong translation. Sure, black holders from behind for the objects could also work, but I will give the "gelatin picture" a try on this weekend, maybe it gives nice watery effects.

Best regards,

Max

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
You could do quite well by using a casting epoxy. I don't think it will change the polarizations but you will want to test it in between crossed polarizers. 

I have had very interesting results making a wavy appearence by passing the reference beam through a wavy optic before mastering.

posts.author: Pianomaxx
posts.content_md:
Hi John,

thanks for your interest! No, I was quite busy at university and didnt have much time. Still, my current aim is to improve the overall brightness of the single-beam holograms, so that I could post nice photos here.

Problem: The pyrogallol processing didnt work well recently, only very slowly, although the recommended processing time was 1min. The exposure time was enough, because with a Hydrochinon+NaOH-Developer ("Dokumol") i got enough density on the plate. My guess is, that the sodium carbonate anhydrous absorbed humidity, so it couldnt work anymore as the basic component, but I will add NaOH instead to speed the reaction up (like it is used in TJ1).

best regards,

Max

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: Max, we used to use pyro developer for transmission holograms years ago and it worked wonderfully but I was never able to get good results from pyro with single beam reflections. Others have more experience and hopefully will chim in with suggestions.
